To survive and flourish, life below the surface has adapted to a sulphuric bacterial foundation, creating a truly unique environment 
far from the light of the sun. Where lakes of acidic water have long ago leaked deeper into the earth, streaks of a blue hued azacrid can 
be found remaining. This oily glimmering stone retains a burn to the touch, even when melted down and forged into a cutting edge. 
Among the stalactites above, in the humid air that carries an abysmal stench, layers of hardened sulfur, mixed with salt and bacterial 
grime can be scraped off and mixed into an oil to coat leather and hide. The yellow speckled oil, infernoil, infuses a slight resistance 
to the acids that make up so much of what lives below. Beyond such unique materials, the tunnels and caves beneath Sol’Kesh harbor 
gardens of fungus and molds that glow and sparkle like the stars above, enticing Travelers to keep venturing deeper.
Expeditions within the Umbrawells
Unearthing What Grows In The Dark
Blind from generations of evolution within the pitch black subterranean 
darkness, the tortoise has developed a highly sensitive horned nose. 
Plodding through the darkness, feasting on bacterial mats and fungal 
molds, confident in its armored shell to protect it from the worst of the 
Umbrawells inhabitants
The blind bassodom utters low frequency sounds that 
reverberate through the fatty tissue of its domed head 
to navigate the black depths with echolocation. Unseen, 
a creeping eerael hag fish encircles the fish, keeping far 
from its front to strike from above
A sickly yellow mat of bacteria feasts 
on the alkaline rich deposits that drip 
from above. When scraped off, it can 
be rendered into infernoil. An acrid 
substance that when spread onto a 
material's surface, offers a surprisingly 
high resistance to acid
